standard_prerequisites.name: Borel maximal independent sets in locally finite Borel graphs
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every locally finite Borel graph admits a Borel maximal independent set.
standard_prerequisites.use: Applied to a locally finite line graph to obtain a maximal matching inside each selected ray-hitting region.

standard_prerequisites.name: Borel finite choices
standard_prerequisites.statement: Finite connected components and finitely many colorings per finite component permit a Borel choice, using a fixed Borel order.
standard_prerequisites.use: Choose alternating two-edge-colorings of finite paths or even cycles; the global disjoint regions and edge cuts are not given.

core_obligations: Construct disjoint Borel two-layer annuli and prove every ray tail crosses each annulus using finite ASI components and local finiteness.
Localize the exceptional third color to a maximal matching in a designated annulus, leaving finite path components.
Share one exceptional color among infinite-generator directions using disjoint annuli, and combine private even-cycle palettes.

proof_roadmap.step: Build annuli from the ASI1 partition and force every ray to cross their successive layers.
Choose exceptional matching edges in the prescribed set and two-color the remaining finite paths.
Separate finite even-order generators from infinite cyclic pairs, then share a single extra color across disjoint regions.

difficulty_reason: The annuli and localized matching mechanism remain nonroutine after Borel finite choices and maximal independent sets. Reuses C-independent H2 opinion; the tail-order clarification is valid.

compared.difference: The published lemma lifts a degree coloring from a quotient by a finite subgroup in the abelian setting. This theorem derives a degree-plus-one coloring directly from ASI1, for arbitrary marked groups without odd-order generators.

editorial_notes: Only the ASI1 degree-plus-one theorem is counted. The two ray/third-color lemmas are proved in full as solution obligations. No theorem establishing ASI1 for particular groups is assumed or counted.
For any ray, the argument applies to every tail, so a point in U0 may be followed by a later point outside its2d-neighborhood when checking the annulus crossings184.
The third color used for different generator pairs occurs only on edges whose endpoints lie in their pairwise disjoint V_i, which is the reason it creates no cross-generator color conflict.

source_authorship.known_AI_disclosure: No AI-assistance declaration located in the read source; no claim about undisclosed workflow.

review_checkpoints: The distance-power threshold4d+1 bounds the path from a chosen U0-neighbor of x_n to one for x_(n+1). A finite U0 component then cannot have an injective ray in a bounded neighborhood.
Maximal matching inside V must occur infinitely in each direction: otherwise far enough along an infinite supply of V-edges, an edge would be disjoint from the matching and could be added.
Free action makes infinite-order generator components bi-infinite paths, even finite-order components even cycles and order2 components single edges.
The final count is |S1|+2d+1=|S|+1, with no overlap between palettes except the deliberately shared third color.
